t:
Section 312(h) of the Housing Act of 1964 is amended—

    (1) 
by striking out “October 31, 1979” and inserting in lieu thereof “November 30, 1979”; and
 
    (2) 
by striking out “November 1, 1979” and inserting in lieu thereof “December 1, 1979”.

fable.w: This section only amends dates in Section 312(h) of the Housing Act of 1964, extending a deadline by one month. There is no tempting reading here: it involves no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government takes part in any federal decision.
fable.s: by striking out “October 31, 1979” and inserting in lieu thereof “November 30, 1979”

opus.w: This section only changes deadline dates in an existing statute. It does not create any process for consulting outside parties, any comment period, hearing, or rulemaking authority, or any right to sue. The fact that it amends a housing program does not add participation that the text itself doesn't contain.
opus.s: by striking out “October 31, 1979” and inserting in lieu thereof “November 30, 1979”
opus.b: Step 1: This section only changes two dates in Section 312(h) of the Housing Act of 1964, a provision that has to do with the rehabilitation loan program. One might be tempted to call it "Yes" because it amends a housing program that could involve regulations. But the amendment itself sets up no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue. It is just a technical date extension.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely amends specific dates in the Housing Act of 1964. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory committees. The changes are administrative deadlines and do not involve any party outside the federal government in a decision-making process.
qwen_chat.s: Section 312(h) of the Housing Act of 1964 is amended— (1) by striking out “October 31, 1979” and inserting in lieu thereof “November 30, 1979”; and (2) by striking out “November 1, 1979” and inserting in lieu thereof “December 1, 1979”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing dates in a statute could implicitly affect participation timelines (e.g., comment periods), but the text itself contains no reference to public input, hearings, or consultation. It is purely a technical amendment to deadlines.
